assessments.reasoning: The English full-text heading at /licenses/pddl/1-0/ names Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL) v1.0. The HTML digest matches 09ecade0250eba538cc68145b8f5448eb44cf8340a414665f7f5c12872102faa. The preamble and §§2–3 directly establish the sequence.

The Index expressly includes public-domain dedications and relevant data, and defines a related legal instrument to include a distinct dedication with a documented licensing connection. PDDL supplies that connection through its data scope and backup licensing terms. The table establishes the criterion without naming or admitting PDDL individually.

challenge.method: Tested a pure dedication reading against §3.3 and an ordinary unconditional license reading against the preamble and §§2.1 and 3.1–3.3. Compared both Index taxonomy rows and tested whether a database-only designation necessarily includes its contents.
challenge.results: Each single-mechanism reading omits operative text. The actual grant makes a license characterization plausible for the fallback, while its express condition and the public-domain purpose support recording the whole instrument as a related dedication. The definition of Work expressly permits a database-only designation.

limitations: The Work can be the specified database, its data, or both. Coverage depends on the rightsholder's designation and rights. Section 2 excludes operating programs, patents and trademarks, and §3.4 recognizes jurisdictional limits on moral-rights waivers.

The taxonomy supports the intended mapping without requiring an exclusive classification across indexes. Active is a proposed lifecycle value. Actual admission, public-domain status of any work, redistribution and installation remain separate questions.
reasoning: The ODC v1.0 preamble states the public-domain purpose and explains why a backup license is needed across jurisdictions. Section 2.1 expressly identifies both mechanisms. Section 3.1 dedicates and relinquishes copyright and database rights. Section 3.2 waives rights and claims if dedication is inapplicable. Section 3.3 grants a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license if both preceding mechanisms are inapplicable. SCES §3 requires preserving those conditions. A distinct dedication for relevant data fits the Index's related-instrument category, with the fallback retained as part of its identity.
